name: Proposition 1.1
description: Let $X$ be a Gaussian random variable with mean $\mu$ and variance $\sigma^2$. Then for any $t > 0$, it holds $\mathbb{P}(X - \mu > t) \leq \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \cdot \frac{e^{-t^2/(2\sigma^2)}}{t}$. By symmetry we also have $\mathbb{P}(X - \mu < -t) \leq \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \cdot \frac{e^{-t^2/(2\sigma^2)}}{t}$, and $\mathbb{P}(|X - \mu| > t) \leq \sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}} \cdot \frac{e^{-t^2/(2\sigma^2)}}{t}$.

name: Lemma 1.3
description: Let $X \sim \mathsf{subG}(\sigma^2)$. Then for any $t > 0$, it holds $$\mathbb{P}[X > t] \leq \exp\left(-\frac{t^2}{2\sigma^2}\right), \quad \text{and} \quad \mathbb{P}[X < -t] \leq \exp\left(-\frac{t^2}{2\sigma^2}\right).$$

name: Lemma 1.4
description: Let $X$ be a random variable such that $\mathbb{P}[|X| > t] \leq 2 \exp\left(-\frac{t^2}{2\sigma^2}\right)$, then for any positive integer $k \geq 1$, $$\mathbb{E}[|X|^k] \leq (2\sigma^2)^{k/2} k \Gamma(k/2).$$ In particular, $$\left(\mathbb{E}[|X|^k]\right)^{1/k} \leq \sigma e^{1/e} \sqrt{k}, \quad k \geq 2,$$ and $\mathbb{E}[|X|] \leq \sigma \sqrt{2\pi}$.

name: Lemma 1.5
description: If (1.3) holds, i.e., $\mathbb{P}[X > t] \leq \exp(-t^2/(2\sigma^2))$ and $\mathbb{P}[X < -t] \leq \exp(-t^2/(2\sigma^2))$ for all $t > 0$, then for any $s > 0$, it holds $$\mathbb{E}[\exp(sX)] \leq e^{4\sigma^2 s^2}.$$

name: Theorem 1.6
description: Let $X = (X_1, \ldots, X_n)$ be a vector of independent sub-Gaussian random variables that have variance proxy $\sigma^2$. Then, the random vector $X$ is sub-Gaussian with variance proxy $\sigma^2$.

name: Corollary 1.7
description: Let $X_1, \ldots, X_n$ be $n$ independent random variables such that $X_i \sim \mathsf{subG}(\sigma^2)$. Then for any $a \in \mathbb{R}^n$, we have $$\mathbb{P}\left[\sum_{i=1}^{n} a_i X_i > t\right] \leq \exp\left(-\frac{t^2}{2\sigma^2 |a|_2^2}\right),$$ and $$\mathbb{P}\left[\sum_{i=1}^{n} a_i X_i < -t\right] \leq \exp\left(-\frac{t^2}{2\sigma^2 |a|_2^2}\right).$$

name: Lemma 1.8 (Hoeffding's lemma (1963))
description: Let $X$ be a random variable such that $\mathbb{E}(X) = 0$ and $X \in [a, b]$ almost surely. Then, for any $s \in \mathbb{R}$, it holds $$\mathbb{E}[e^{sX}] \leq e^{s^2(b-a)^2/8}.$$ In particular, $X \sim \mathsf{subG}\!\left(\frac{(b-a)^2}{4}\right)$.

name: Theorem 1.9 (Hoeffding's inequality)
description: Let $X_1, \ldots, X_n$ be $n$ independent random variables such that almost surely, $X_i \in [a_i, b_i]$ for all $i$. Let $\bar{X} = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^{n} X_i$, then for any $t > 0$, $$\mathbb{P}(\bar{X} - \mathbb{E}(\bar{X}) > t) \leq \exp\left(-\frac{2n^2 t^2}{\sum_{i=1}^n (b_i - a_i)^2}\right),$$ and $$\mathbb{P}(\bar{X} - \mathbb{E}(\bar{X}) < -t) \leq \exp\left(-\frac{2n^2 t^2}{\sum_{i=1}^n (b_i - a_i)^2}\right).$$

name: Lemma 1.10
description: Let $X$ be a centered random variable such that $\mathbb{P}(|X| > t) \leq 2e^{-2t/\lambda}$ for some $\lambda > 0$. Then, for any positive integer $k \geq 1$, $$\mathbb{E}[|X|^k] \leq \lambda^k k!.$$ Moreover, $$\left(\mathbb{E}[|X|^k]\right)^{1/k} \leq 2\lambda k,$$ and the moment generating function of $X$ satisfies $$\mathbb{E}\left[e^{sX}\right] \leq e^{2s^2\lambda^2}, \qquad \forall\, |s| \leq \frac{1}{2\lambda}.$$

name: Lemma 1.12
description: Let $X \sim \mathsf{subG}(\sigma^2)$. Then the random variable $Z = X^2 - \mathbb{E}[X^2]$ is sub-exponential: $Z \sim \mathsf{subE}(16\sigma^2)$.

name: Theorem 1.13 (Bernstein's inequality)
description: Let $X_1, \ldots, X_n$ be independent random variables such that $\mathbb{E}(X_i) = 0$ and $X_i \sim \mathsf{subE}(\lambda)$. Define $\bar{X} = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^{n} X_i$. Then for any $t > 0$ we have $$\mathbb{P}(\bar{X} > t) \vee \mathbb{P}(\bar{X} < -t) \leq \exp\left[-\frac{n}{2}\left(\frac{t^2}{\lambda^2} \wedge \frac{t}{\lambda}\right)\right].$$

name: Theorem 1.14
description: Let $X_1, \ldots, X_N$ be $N$ random variables such that $X_i \sim \mathsf{subG}(\sigma^2)$. Then $$\mathbb{E}\!\left[\max_{1 \leq i \leq N} X_i\right] \leq \sigma \sqrt{2 \log(N)}, \quad \text{and} \quad \mathbb{E}\!\left[\max_{1 \leq i \leq N} |X_i|\right] \leq \sigma \sqrt{2 \log(2N)}.$$ Moreover, for any $t > 0$, $$\mathbb{P}\!\left(\max_{1 \leq i \leq N} X_i > t\right) \leq N e^{-t^2/(2\sigma^2)}, \quad \text{and} \quad \mathbb{P}\!\left(\max_{1 \leq i \leq N} |X_i| > t\right) \leq 2N e^{-t^2/(2\sigma^2)}.$$ Note that the random variables in this theorem need not be independent.

name: Lemma 1.15
description: Consider a linear form $x \mapsto c^\top x$, $x, c \in \mathbb{R}^d$. Then for any convex polytope $\mathsf{P} \subset \mathbb{R}^d$, $$\max_{x \in \mathsf{P}} c^\top x = \max_{x \in \mathcal{V}(\mathsf{P})} c^\top x$$ where $\mathcal{V}(\mathsf{P})$ denotes the set of vertices of $\mathsf{P}$.

name: Theorem 1.16
description: Let $\mathsf{P}$ be a polytope with $N$ vertices $v^{(1)}, \ldots, v^{(N)} \in \mathbb{R}^d$ and let $X \in \mathbb{R}^d$ be a random vector such that $[v^{(i)}]^\top X$, $i = 1, \ldots, N$ are sub-Gaussian random variables with variance proxy $\sigma^2$. Then $$\mathbb{E}\!\left[\max_{\theta \in \mathsf{P}} \theta^\top X\right] \leq \sigma \sqrt{2 \log(N)}, \quad \text{and} \quad \mathbb{E}\!\left[\max_{\theta \in \mathsf{P}} |\theta^\top X|\right] \leq \sigma \sqrt{2 \log(2N)}.$$ Moreover, for any $t > 0$, $$\mathbb{P}\!\left(\max_{\theta \in \mathsf{P}} \theta^\top X > t\right) \leq N e^{-t^2/(2\sigma^2)}, \quad \text{and} \quad \mathbb{P}\!\left(\max_{\theta \in \mathsf{P}} |\theta^\top X| > t\right) \leq 2N e^{-t^2/(2\sigma^2)}.$$

name: Lemma 1.18
description: Fix $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$. Then the unit Euclidean ball $\mathcal{B}_2$ has an $\varepsilon$-net $\mathcal{N}$ with respect to the Euclidean distance of cardinality $|\mathcal{N}| \leq (3/\varepsilon)^d$.

name: Theorem 1.19
description: Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^d$ be a sub-Gaussian random vector with variance proxy $\sigma^2$. Then $$\mathbb{E}\!\left[\max_{\theta \in \mathcal{B}_2} \theta^\top X\right] = \mathbb{E}\!\left[\max_{\theta \in \mathcal{B}_2} |\theta^\top X|\right] \leq 4\sigma\sqrt{d}.$$ Moreover, for any $\delta > 0$, with probability $1 - \delta$, it holds $$\max_{\theta \in \mathcal{B}_2} \theta^\top X = \max_{\theta \in \mathcal{B}_2} |\theta^\top X| \leq 4\sigma \sqrt{d} + 2\sigma \sqrt{2\log(1/\delta)}.$$

name: Proposition 2.1
description: The least squares estimator $\hat{\mu}^{\mathrm{LS}} = \mathbb{X}\hat{\theta}^{\mathrm{LS}} \in \mathbb{R}^n$ satisfies $\mathbb{X}^{\top} \hat{\mu}^{\mathrm{LS}} = \mathbb{X}^{\top} Y$. Moreover, $\hat{\theta}^{\mathrm{LS}}$ can be chosen to be $\hat{\theta}^{\mathrm{LS}} = (\mathbb{X}^{\top} \mathbb{X})^{\dagger} \mathbb{X}^{\top} Y$, where $(\mathbb{X}^{\top}\mathbb{X})^{\dagger}$ denotes the Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse of $\mathbb{X}^{\top}\mathbb{X}$.

name: Theorem 2.2
description: Assume that the linear model (2.2) holds where $\varepsilon \sim \mathsf{subG}_n(\sigma^2)$. Then the least squares estimator $\hat{\theta}^{\mathrm{LS}}$ satisfies $$\mathbb{E}\!\left[\mathsf{MSE}(\mathbb{X}\hat{\theta}^{\mathrm{LS}})\right] = \frac{1}{n}\mathbb{E}|\mathbb{X}\hat{\theta}^{\mathrm{LS}} - \mathbb{X}\theta^*|_2^2 \lesssim \sigma^2 \frac{r}{n},$$ where $r = \operatorname{rank}(\mathbb{X}^{\top}\mathbb{X})$. Moreover, for any $\delta > 0$, with probability $1 - \delta$, it holds $$\mathsf{MSE}(\mathbb{X}\hat{\theta}^{\mathrm{LS}}) \lesssim \sigma^2 \frac{r + \log(1/\delta)}{n}.$$

name: Theorem 2.4
description: Let $K = \mathcal{B}_1$ be the unit $\ell_1$ ball of $\mathbb{R}^d$, $d \geq 2$ and assume that $\theta^* \in \mathcal{B}_1$. Moreover, assume the conditions of Theorem 2.2 and that the columns of $\mathbb{X}$ are normalized in such a way that $\max_j |\mathbb{X}_j|_2 \leq \sqrt{n}$. Then the constrained least squares estimator $\hat{\theta}_{\mathcal{B}_1}^{\mathrm{LS}}$ satisfies $$\mathbb{E}\!\left[\mathsf{MSE}(\mathbb{X}\hat{\theta}_{\mathcal{B}_1}^{\mathrm{LS}})\right] = \frac{1}{n}\mathbb{E}|\mathbb{X}\hat{\theta}_{\mathcal{B}_1}^{\mathrm{LS}} - \mathbb{X}\theta^*|_2^2 \lesssim \sigma\sqrt{\frac{\log d}{n}}.$$ Moreover, for any $\delta > 0$, with probability $1 - \delta$, it holds $$\mathsf{MSE}(\mathbb{X}\hat{\theta}^{\mathrm{LS}}_{\mathcal{B}_1}) \lesssim \sigma \sqrt{\frac{\log(d/\delta)}{n}}.$$

name: Theorem 2.6
description: Fix a positive integer $k \leq d/2$. Let $K = \mathcal{B}_0(k)$ be the set of $k$-sparse vectors of $\mathbb{R}^d$ and assume that $\theta^* \in \mathcal{B}_0(k)$. Moreover, assume the conditions of Theorem 2.2. Then, for any $\delta > 0$, with probability $1 - \delta$, it holds $$\mathsf{MSE}(\mathbb{X}\hat{\theta}_{\mathcal{B}_0(k)}^{\mathrm{LS}}) \lesssim \frac{\sigma^2}{n} \log \binom{d}{2k} + \frac{\sigma^2 k}{n} + \frac{\sigma^2}{n} \log(1/\delta).$$

name: Lemma 2.7
description: For any integers $1 \leq k \leq n$, it holds $\binom{n}{k} \leq \left(\frac{en}{k}\right)^k$.

name: Corollary 2.8
description: Under the assumptions of Theorem 2.6, for any $\delta > 0$, with probability $1 - \delta$, it holds $$\mathsf{MSE}(\mathbb{X}\hat{\theta}_{\mathcal{B}_0(k)}^{\mathrm{LS}}) \lesssim \frac{\sigma^2 k}{n} \log\!\left(\frac{ed}{2k}\right) + \frac{\sigma^2 k}{n} \log(6) + \frac{\sigma^2}{n} \log(1/\delta).$$

name: Corollary 2.9
description: Under the assumptions of Theorem 2.6, $$\mathbb{E}\!\left[\mathsf{MSE}(\mathbb{X}\hat{\theta}_{\mathcal{B}_0(k)}^{\mathrm{LS}})\right] \lesssim \frac{\sigma^2 k}{n} \log \!\left(\frac{ed}{k}\right).$$

name: Theorem 2.11
description: Consider the linear regression model (2.2) under the assumption ORT or, equivalently, the sub-Gaussian sequence model (2.9). Then the hard thresholding estimator $\hat{\theta}^{\mathrm{HRD}}$ with threshold $2\tau = 2\sigma\sqrt{2 \log(2d/\delta)/n}$ enjoys the following two properties on the same event $A$ such that $\mathbb{P}(A) \geq 1 - \delta$: (i) If $|\theta^*|_0 = k$, $\mathsf{MSE}(\mathbb{X}\hat{\theta}^{\mathrm{HRD}}) = |\hat{\theta}^{\mathrm{HRD}} - \theta^*|_2^2 \lesssim \sigma^2 k \log(2d/\delta)/n$. (ii) If $\min_{j \in \operatorname{supp}(\theta^*)} |\theta^*_j| > 3\tau$, then $\operatorname{supp}(\hat{\theta}^{\mathrm{HRD}}) = \operatorname{supp}(\theta^*)$.

name: Theorem 2.14
description: Assume that the linear model (2.2) holds where $\varepsilon \sim \mathsf{subG}_n(\sigma^2)$. Then, the BIC estimator $\hat{\theta}^{\mathrm{BIC}}$ with regularization parameter $\tau^2 = 16 \log(6) \sigma^2/n + 32 \sigma^2 \log(ed)/n$ satisfies $$\mathsf{MSE}(\mathbb{X}\hat{\theta}^{\mathrm{BIC}}) = \frac{1}{n}|\mathbb{X}\hat{\theta}^{\mathrm{BIC}} - \mathbb{X}\theta^*|_2^2 \lesssim |\theta^*|_0 \frac{\sigma^2 \log(ed/\delta)}{n}$$ with probability at least $1 - \delta$.

name: Theorem 2.15
description: Assume that the linear model (2.2) holds where $\varepsilon \sim \mathsf{subG}_n(\sigma^2)$. Moreover, assume that the columns of $\mathbb{X}$ are normalized in such a way that $\max_j |\mathbb{X}_j|_2 \leq \sqrt{n}$. Then, the Lasso estimator $\hat{\theta}^{\mathrm{L}}$ with regularization parameter $2\tau = 2\sigma\sqrt{2 \log(2d)/n} + 2\sigma\sqrt{2 \log(1/\delta)/n}$ satisfies $$\mathsf{MSE}(\mathbb{X}\hat{\theta}^{\mathrm{L}}) = \frac{1}{n}|\mathbb{X}\hat{\theta}^{\mathrm{L}} - \mathbb{X}\theta^*|_2^2 \leq 4|\theta^*|_1 \sigma\sqrt{\frac{2 \log(2d)}{n}} + 4|\theta^*|_1 \sigma\sqrt{\frac{2 \log(1/\delta)}{n}}$$ with probability at least $1 - \delta$. Moreover, there exists a numerical constant $C > 0$ such that $\mathbb{E}[\mathsf{MSE}(\mathbb{X}\hat{\theta}^{\mathrm{L}})] \leq C |\theta^*|_1 \sigma\sqrt{\log(2d)/n}$.

name: Proposition 2.16
description: Let $\mathbb{X} \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times d}$ be a random matrix with entries $X_{ij}$, $i = 1, \ldots, n$, $j = 1, \ldots, d$ that are i.i.d. Rademacher $(\pm 1)$ random variables. Then, $\mathbb{X}$ has incoherence $k$ with probability $1 - \delta$ as soon as $n \geq 392 k^2 \log(1/\delta) + 784 k^2 \log(d)$. It implies that there exist matrices that satisfy Assumption $\mathrm{INC}(k)$ for $n \gtrsim k^2 \log(d)$.

name: Lemma 2.17
description: Fix a positive integer $k \leq d$ and assume that $\mathbb{X}$ satisfies assumption $\mathrm{INC}(k)$. Then, for any $S \subset \{1, \ldots, d\}$ such that $|S| \leq k$ and any $\theta \in \mathbb{R}^d$ that satisfies the cone condition $|\theta_{S^c}|_1 \leq 3|\theta_S|_1$, it holds $|\theta_S|_2^2 \leq 2 |\mathbb{X}\theta|_2^2 / n$.

name: Theorem 2.18
description: Fix $n \geq 2$. Assume that the linear model (2.2) holds where $\varepsilon \sim \mathsf{subG}_n(\sigma^2)$. Moreover, assume that $|\theta^*|_0 \leq k$ and that $\mathbb{X}$ satisfies assumption $\mathrm{INC}(k)$. Then the Lasso estimator $\hat{\theta}^{\mathrm{L}}$ with regularization parameter $2\tau = 8\sigma\sqrt{\log(2d)/n} + 8\sigma\sqrt{\log(1/\delta)/n}$ satisfies $$\mathsf{MSE}(\mathbb{X}\hat{\theta}^{\mathrm{L}}) = \frac{1}{n}|\mathbb{X}\hat{\theta}^{\mathrm{L}} - \mathbb{X}\theta^*|_2^2 \lesssim \frac{k \sigma^2 \log(2d/\delta)}{n}$$ and $|\hat{\theta}^{\mathrm{L}} - \theta^*|_1 \lesssim k\sigma\sqrt{\log(2d/\delta)/n}$ with probability at least $1 - \delta$. Moreover, $\mathbb{E}[\mathsf{MSE}(\mathbb{X}\hat{\theta}^{\mathrm{L}})] \lesssim k \sigma^2 \log(2d)/n$ and $\mathbb{E}[|\hat{\theta}^{\mathrm{L}} - \theta^*|_1] \lesssim k\sigma\sqrt{\log(2d/\delta)/n}$.

name: Theorem 3.3
description: Assume the general regression model (3.1) with $\varepsilon \sim \mathsf{subG}_n(\sigma^2)$. Then, the least squares estimator $\hat{\theta}^{\mathrm{LS}}$ satisfies for some numerical constant $C > 0$, $$\mathsf{MSE}(\varphi_{\hat{\theta}^{\mathrm{LS}}}) \leq \inf_{\theta \in \mathbb{R}^M} \mathsf{MSE}(\varphi_\theta) + C \sigma^2 \frac{M}{n} \cdot \log(1/\delta)$$ with probability at least $1 - \delta$.

name: Theorem 3.4
description: Assume the general regression model (3.1) with $\varepsilon \sim \mathsf{subG}_n(\sigma^2)$. Then, the BIC estimator $\hat{\theta}^{\mathrm{BIC}}$ with regularization parameter $\tau^2 = 16\sigma^2/(\alpha n) \log(6eM)$, $\alpha \in (0,1)$ satisfies for some numerical constant $C > 0$, $$\mathsf{MSE}(\varphi_{\hat{\theta}^{\mathrm{BIC}}}) \leq \inf_{\theta \in \mathbb{R}^M} \left\{ \frac{1+\alpha}{1-\alpha} \mathsf{MSE}(\varphi_\theta) + \frac{C\sigma^2}{\alpha(1-\alpha)n} |\theta|_0 \log(eM) \right\} + \frac{C\sigma^2}{\alpha(1-\alpha)n} \log(1/\delta)$$ with probability at least $1 - \delta$.

name: Theorem 3.5
description: Assume the general regression model (3.1) with $\varepsilon \sim \mathsf{subG}_n(\sigma^2)$. Moreover, assume that there exists an integer $k$ such that the matrix $\Phi$ satisfies assumption $\mathrm{INC}(k)$. Then, the Lasso estimator $\hat{\theta}^{\mathrm{L}}$ with regularization parameter $2\tau = 8\sigma\sqrt{2\log(2M)/n} + 8\sigma\sqrt{2\log(1/\delta)/n}$ satisfies for some numerical constant $C$, $$\mathsf{MSE}(\varphi_{\hat{\theta}^{\mathrm{L}}}) \leq \inf_{\theta \in \mathbb{R}^M,\, |\theta|_0 \leq k} \left\{ \frac{1+\alpha}{1-\alpha} \mathsf{MSE}(\varphi_\theta) + \frac{C\sigma^2}{\alpha(1-\alpha)n} |\theta|_0 \log(eM) \right\} + \frac{C\sigma^2}{\alpha(1-\alpha)n} \log(1/\delta)$$ with probability at least $1 - \delta$.

name: Theorem 3.6
description: Let $\{\varphi_1, \ldots, \varphi_M\}$ be a dictionary normalized in such a way that $\max_{1 \leq j \leq M} |\varphi_j|_2 \leq D\sqrt{n}$. Then for any integer $k$ such that $1 \leq k \leq M$ and any positive $R$, we have $$\min_{\theta \in \mathbb{R}^M,\, |\theta|_0 \leq 2k} \mathsf{MSE}(\varphi_\theta) \leq \min_{\theta \in \mathbb{R}^M,\, |\theta|_1 \leq R} \mathsf{MSE}(\varphi_\theta) + D^2 R^2 / k.$$

name: Corollary 3.7
description: Assume that the assumptions of Theorem 3.4 hold and that the dictionary $\{\varphi_1, \ldots, \varphi_M\}$ is normalized in such a way that $\max_{1 \leq j \leq M} |\varphi_j|_2 \leq \sqrt{n}$. Then there exists a constant $C > 0$ such that the BIC estimator satisfies $$\mathsf{MSE}(\varphi_{\hat{\theta}^{\mathrm{BIC}}}) \leq \inf_{\theta \in \mathbb{R}^M} \left\{ 2\, \mathsf{MSE}(\varphi_\theta) + C \left[ \frac{\sigma^2 |\theta|_0 \log(eM)}{n} \wedge \sigma |\theta|_1 \sqrt{\frac{\log(eM)}{n}} \right] \right\} + \frac{C \sigma^2 \log(1/\delta)}{n}$$ with probability at least $1 - \delta$.

name: Theorem 3.11
description: Fix $\beta \geq 1$ and $L > 0$ and let $\{\varphi_j\}_{j \geq 1}$ denote the trigonometric basis of $L_2([0,1])$. Moreover, let $\{a_j\}_{j \geq 1}$ be defined as in (3.9). A function $f \in W(\beta, L)$ can be represented as $f = \sum_{j=1}^{\infty} \theta_j^* \varphi_j$, where the sequence $\{\theta_j^*\}_{j \geq 1}$ belongs to the Sobolev ellipsoid of $\ell_2(\mathbb{N})$ defined by $\Theta(\beta, Q) = \{ \theta \in \ell_2(\mathbb{N}) \mid \sum_{j=1}^{\infty} a_j^2 \theta_j^2 \leq Q \}$ for $Q = L^2 / \pi^{2\beta}$.

name: Proposition 3.12
location: Chapter 3, Section on Sobolev classes and ellipsoids
description: The Sobolev ellipsoids enjoy the following properties: (i) For any $Q > 0$, $0 < \beta' < \beta$ implies $\Theta(\beta, Q) \subset \Theta(\beta', Q)$. (ii) For any $Q > 0$, $\beta > 1/2$ implies $f$ is continuous.

name: Lemma 3.13
location: Chapter 3, Section on Sobolev classes and ellipsoids
description: Assume that $\{X_1, \ldots, X_n\}$ is the regular design, i.e., $X_i = (i-1)/n$. Then, for any $M \leq n-1$, the design matrix $\Phi = \{\varphi_j(X_i)\}_{1 \leq i \leq n,\, 1 \leq j \leq M}$ satisfies the ORT condition.

name: Lemma 3.14
location: Chapter 3, Section on Integrated squared error
description: For any integer $M \geq 1$, and $f \in \Theta(\beta, Q)$, $\beta > 1/2$, it holds $$\|\varphi_{\theta^*}^M - f\|_{L_2}^2 = \sum_{j > M} |\theta_j^*|^2 \leq Q M^{-2\beta},$$ and for $M = n-1$, we have $|\varphi_{\theta^*}^{n-1} - f|_2^2 \leq 2n\!\left(\sum_{j \geq n} |\theta_j^*|\right)^2 \lesssim Q n^{2-2\beta}$.

name: Theorem 3.15
location: Chapter 3, Section on Integrated squared error
description: Fix $\beta \geq (1+\sqrt{5})/4 \approx 0.81$, $Q > 0$, $\delta > 0$ and assume the general regression model (3.1) with $f \in \Theta(\beta, Q)$ and $\varepsilon \sim \mathsf{subG}_n(\sigma^2)$, $\sigma^2 \leq 1$. Moreover, let $M = \lceil n^{1/(2\beta+1)} \rceil$ and $n$ be large enough so that $M \leq n-1$. Then the least squares estimator $\hat{\theta}^{\mathrm{LS}}$ defined in (3.2) with $\{\varphi_j\}_{j=1}^M$ being the trigonometric basis, satisfies with probability $1-\delta$, for $n$ large enough, $$\|\varphi_{\hat{\theta}^{\mathrm{LS}}} - f\|_{L_2([0,1])}^2 \lesssim n^{-2\beta/(2\beta+1)} + \sigma^2 \log(1/\delta)/n,$$ where the constant factors may depend on $\beta$, $Q$ and $\sigma$. Moreover $\mathbb{E}\|\varphi_{\hat{\theta}^{\mathrm{LS}}} - f\|_{L_2([0,1])}^2 \lesssim n^{-2\beta/(2\beta+1)}$.

name: Corollary 3.16
description: Fix $\beta \geq (1+\sqrt{5})/4 \approx 0.81$, $Q > 0$, $\delta > 0$ and $n$ large enough to ensure $n-1 \geq \lceil n^{1/(2\beta+1)} \rceil$, assume the general regression model (3.1) with $f \in \Theta(\beta, Q)$ and $\varepsilon \sim \mathsf{subG}_n(\sigma^2)$, $\sigma^2 \leq 1$. Let $\{\varphi_j\}_{j=1}^{n-1}$ be the trigonometric basis. Denote by $\varphi_{\hat{\theta}^{\mathrm{BIC}}}^{n-1}$ (resp. $\varphi_{\hat{\theta}^{\mathrm{L}}}^{n-1}$) the BIC (resp. Lasso) estimator defined in (3.3) (resp. (3.4)) over $\mathbb{R}^{n-1}$ with regularization parameter given by (3.5) (resp. (3.6)). Then $\varphi_{\hat{\theta}}^{n-1}$, where $\hat{\theta} \in \{\hat{\theta}^{\mathrm{BIC}}, \hat{\theta}^{\mathrm{L}}\}$ satisfies with probability $1-\delta$, $$\|\varphi_{\hat{\theta}}^{n-1} - f\|_{L_2([0,1])}^2 \lesssim n^{-2\beta/(2\beta+1)} + \sigma^2 \log(1/\delta)/n.$$ Moreover, $\mathbb{E}\|\varphi_{\hat{\theta}}^{n-1} - f\|_{L_2([0,1])}^2 \lesssim \sigma^2 (\log n / n)^{2\beta/(2\beta+1)}$, where constant factors may depend on $\beta$ and $Q$.

name: Lemma 4.2
location: Chapter 4, Section 4.2 (Multivariate regression, Sub-Gaussian matrix model)
description: Let $A$ be a $d \times T$ random matrix such that $A \sim \mathsf{subG}_{d \times T}(\sigma^2)$. Then $\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}} \leq 4\sigma\sqrt{\log(12)(d \vee T)} + 2\sigma\sqrt{2 \log(1/\delta)}$ with probability $1 - \delta$.

name: Theorem 4.3
description: Consider the multivariate linear regression model (4.1) under the assumption ORT or, equivalently, the sub-Gaussian matrix model (4.2). Then, the singular value thresholding estimator $\hat{\Theta}^{\mathrm{SVT}}$ with threshold $$2\tau = 8\sigma\sqrt{\frac{\log(12)(d \vee T)}{n}} + 4\sigma\sqrt{\frac{2\log(1/\delta)}{n}},$$ satisfies $$\frac{1}{n} \|\mathbb{X}\hat{\Theta}^{\mathrm{SVT}} - \mathbb{X}\Theta^*\|_F^2 = \|\hat{\Theta}^{\mathrm{SVT}} - \Theta^*\|_F^2 \leq 144 \operatorname{rank}(\Theta^*) \tau^2 \lesssim \frac{\sigma^2 \operatorname{rank}(\Theta^*)}{n} \left( d \vee T + \log(1/\delta) \right)$$ with probability $1 - \delta$.

name: Theorem 4.4
description: Consider the multivariate linear regression model (4.1). Then, the estimator by rank penalization $\hat{\Theta}^{\mathrm{RK}}$ with regularization parameter $\tau^2$, where $\tau$ is defined in (4.3) satisfies $$\frac{1}{n} \|\mathbb{X}\hat{\Theta}^{\mathrm{RK}} - \mathbb{X}\Theta^*\|_F^2 \leq 8 \operatorname{rank}(\Theta^*) \tau^2 \lesssim \frac{\sigma^2 \operatorname{rank}(\Theta^*)}{n} \left( d \vee T + \log(1/\delta) \right)$$ with probability $1 - \delta$.

name: Theorem 4.6
description: Let $X_1, \ldots, X_n$ be $n$ i.i.d. sub-Gaussian random vectors such that $\mathbb{E}[XX^{\top}] = \Sigma$ and $X \sim \mathsf{subG}_d(\|\Sigma\|_{\mathrm{op}})$. Then $$\|\hat{\Sigma} - \Sigma\|_{\mathrm{op}} \lesssim \|\Sigma\|_{\mathrm{op}} \left(\sqrt{\frac{d + \log(1/\delta)}{n}} \vee \frac{d + \log(1/\delta)}{n}\right)$$ with probability $1 - \delta$.

name: Theorem 4.8 (Davis-Kahan $\sin(\theta)$ theorem)
description: Let $\Sigma$ satisfy the spiked covariance model and let $\tilde{\Sigma}$ be any PSD estimator of $\Sigma$. Let $\tilde{v}$ denote the largest eigenvector of $\tilde{\Sigma}$. Then we have $$\min_{\varepsilon \in \{\pm 1\}} |\varepsilon \tilde{v} - v|_2^2 \leq 2 \sin^2\!\left(\angle(\tilde{v}, v)\right) \leq \frac{8}{\theta^2} \|\tilde{\Sigma} - \Sigma\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2.$$

name: Corollary 4.9
description: Let $X_1, \ldots, X_n$ be $n$ i.i.d. copies of a sub-Gaussian random vector $X \in \mathbb{R}^d$ such that $\mathbb{E}[XX^\top] = \Sigma$ and $X \sim \mathsf{subG}_d(\|\Sigma\|_{\mathrm{op}})$. Assume further that $\Sigma = \theta vv^\top + I_d$ satisfies the spiked covariance model. Then, the largest eigenvector $\hat{v}$ of the empirical covariance matrix $\hat{\Sigma}$ satisfies, $$\min_{\varepsilon \in \{\pm 1\}} |\varepsilon \hat{v} - v|_2 \lesssim \frac{1+\theta}{\theta} \left(\sqrt{\frac{d + \log(1/\delta)}{n}} \vee \frac{d + \log(1/\delta)}{n}\right)$$ with probability $1 - \delta$.

name: Theorem 4.10
description: Let $X_1, \ldots, X_n$ be $n$ i.i.d. copies of a sub-Gaussian random vector $X \in \mathbb{R}^d$ such that $\mathbb{E}[XX^\top] = \Sigma$ and $X \sim \mathsf{subG}_d(\|\Sigma\|_{\mathrm{op}})$. Assume further that $\Sigma = \theta vv^\top + I_d$ satisfies the spiked covariance model for $v$ such that $|v|_0 = k \leq d/2$. Then, the $k$-sparse largest eigenvector $\hat{v}$ of the empirical covariance matrix satisfies, $$\min_{\varepsilon \in \{\pm 1\}} |\varepsilon \hat{v} - v|_2 \lesssim \frac{1 + \theta}{\theta} \left(\sqrt{\frac{k \log(ed/k) + \log(1/\delta)}{n}} \vee \frac{k \log(ed/k) + \log(1/\delta)}{n}\right)$$ with probability $1 - \delta$.

name: Lemma 5.3 (Neyman-Pearson)
description: Let $\mathbb{P}_0$ and $\mathbb{P}_1$ be two probability measures. Then for any test $\psi$, it holds $$\mathbb{P}_0(\psi = 1) + \mathbb{P}_1(\psi = 0) \geq \int \min(p_0, p_1).$$ Moreover, equality holds for the Likelihood Ratio test $\psi^* = \mathbb{I}(p_1 \geq p_0)$.

name: Proposition 5.6
description: Let $\mathbb{P}$ and $\mathbb{Q}$ be two probability measures. Then 1. $\mathsf{KL}(\mathbb{P}, \mathbb{Q}) \geq 0$. 2. If $\mathbb{P}$ and $\mathbb{Q}$ are product measures, i.e., $\mathbb{P} = \bigotimes_{i=1}^{n} \mathbb{P}_i$ and $\mathbb{Q} = \bigotimes_{i=1}^{n} \mathbb{Q}_i$, then $\mathsf{KL}(\mathbb{P}, \mathbb{Q}) = \sum_{i=1}^{n} \mathsf{KL}(\mathbb{P}_{i}, \mathbb{Q}_{i})$.

name: Lemma 5.8 (Pinsker's inequality)
description: Let $\mathbb{P}$ and $\mathbb{Q}$ be two probability measures such that $\mathbb{P} \ll \mathbb{Q}$. Then $$\mathsf{TV}(\mathbb{P}, \mathbb{Q}) \leq \sqrt{\mathsf{KL}(\mathbb{P}, \mathbb{Q})}.$$

name: Theorem 5.9
description: Assume that $\Theta$ contains two hypotheses $\theta_0$ and $\theta_1$ such that $|\theta_0 - \theta_1|_2^2 = 8\alpha^2\sigma^2/n$ for some $\alpha \in (0, 1/2)$. Then $$\inf_{\hat{\theta}} \sup_{\theta \in \Theta} \mathbb{P}_{\theta}\!\left(|\hat{\theta} - \theta|_2^2 \geq \frac{2\alpha\sigma^2}{n}\right) \geq \frac{1}{2} - \alpha.$$

name: Theorem 5.10 (Fano's inequality)
description: Let $P_1, \ldots, P_M$, $M \geq 2$ be probability distributions such that $P_j \ll P_k$ for all $j, k$. Then $$\inf_{\psi} \max_{1 \leq j \leq M} P_j\!\left[\psi(X) \neq j\right] \geq 1 - \frac{\frac{1}{M^2} \sum_{j,k=1}^{M} \mathsf{KL}(P_j, P_k) + \log 2}{\log(M - 1)}$$ where the infimum is taken over all tests with values in $\{1, \ldots, M\}$.

name: Theorem 5.11
description: Assume that $\Theta$ contains $M \geq 5$ hypotheses $\theta_1, \ldots, \theta_M$ such that for some constant $0 < \alpha < 1/4$, it holds (i) $|\theta_j - \theta_k|_2^2 \geq 4\phi$ and (ii) $|\theta_j - \theta_k|_2^2 \leq \frac{2\alpha\sigma^2}{n}\log(M)$. Then $$\inf_{\hat{\theta}} \sup_{\theta \in \Theta} \mathbb{P}_{\theta}\!\left(|\hat{\theta} - \theta|_2^2 \geq \phi\right) \geq \frac{1}{2} - 2\alpha.$$

name: Lemma 5.12 (Varshamov-Gilbert)
description: For any $\gamma \in (0, 1/2)$, there exist binary vectors $\omega_1, \ldots, \omega_M \in \{0, 1\}^d$ such that (i) $\rho(\omega_j, \omega_k) \geq \left(\frac{1}{2} - \gamma\right) d$ for all $j \neq k$, and (ii) $M = \lfloor e^{\gamma^2 d} \rfloor \geq e^{\gamma^2 d / 2}$.

name: Corollary 5.13
description: The minimax rate of estimation over $\mathbb{R}^d$ in the Gaussian sequence model is $\phi(\mathbb{R}^d) = \sigma^2 d/n$. Moreover, it is attained by the least squares estimator $\hat{\theta}^{\mathrm{LS}} = \mathbf{Y}$.

name: Lemma 5.14 (Sparse Varshamov-Gilbert)
description: There exist positive constants $C_1$ and $C_2$ such that the following holds for any two integers $k$ and $d$ such that $1 \leq k \leq d/8$. There exist binary vectors $\omega_1, \ldots, \omega_M \in \{0, 1\}^d$ such that (i) $\rho(\omega_i, \omega_j) \geq k/2$ for all $i \neq j$, (ii) $\log(M) \geq \frac{k}{8} \log\!\left(1 + \frac{d}{2k}\right)$, and (iii) $|\omega_j|_0 = k$ for all $j$.

name: Corollary 5.15
description: Recall that $\mathcal{B}_0(k) \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ denotes the set of all $k$-sparse vectors of $\mathbb{R}^d$. The minimax rate of estimation over $\mathcal{B}_0(k)$ in the Gaussian sequence model is $\phi(\mathcal{B}_0(k)) = \frac{\sigma^2 k}{n} \log(ed/k)$. Moreover, it is attained by the constrained least squares estimator $\hat{\theta}_{\mathcal{B}_0(k)}^{\mathrm{LS}}$.

name: Corollary 5.16
description: Recall that $\mathcal{B}_1(R) \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ denotes the set of vectors $\theta \in \mathbb{R}^d$ such that $|\theta|_1 \leq R$. Then there exists a constant $C > 0$ such that if $d \geq n^{1/2+\varepsilon}$, $\varepsilon > 0$, the minimax rate of estimation over $\mathcal{B}_1(R)$ in the Gaussian sequence model is $\phi(\mathcal{B}_1(R)) = \min(R^2,\, R\sigma \log d / n)$. Moreover, it is attained by the constrained least squares estimator $\hat{\theta}_{\mathcal{B}_1(R)}^{\mathrm{LS}}$ if $R \geq \sigma \log d / n$ and by the trivial estimator $\hat{\theta} = 0$ otherwise.
